# Hash-pinned install set for the three desktop bundle jobs.
#
# Direct requirements: pystray Pillow pywebview PyGObject pyinstaller
#                      certifi truststore
#                      (i.e. the closure of desktop/requirements-dev.txt)
#
# Used by desktop-artifacts.yml's macos, windows and linux jobs, each of
# which ran `pip install -r desktop/requirements-dev.txt` against a file
# whose every line is a FLOOR (`>=`), not a pin. Those three jobs are not
# ordinary CI: their output is the signed .dmg / .exe / .deb / .AppImage a
# user downloads and runs. Everything the resolver picked at build time is
# frozen into that bundle by PyInstaller and then signed, so an unpinned
# resolve here is the one place in this repo where "whatever the index
# served that minute" ends up on an end user's machine over our signature.
# pyinstaller is the bundler itself and pywebview/PyGObject/pystray are the
# native shell; there is no later step that would notice a substitution.
#
# The pip + wheel bootstrap above each of these installs was already
# hash-pinned (pip-wheel-bootstrap.txt), and that file's header names this
# gap explicitly -- it exists because desktop/requirements-dev.txt pulls
# PyGObject, an sdist-only build on Linux. This file closes the other half:
# the bootstrap pins the tool, and this pins what the tool installs.
#
# desktop/requirements-dev.txt stays in the tree and keeps its floors. It
# is what a developer installs to run `python -m desktop.tray` locally, and
# it carries the long-form reasoning for each floor (the PyGObject 3.58.0
# note in particular). This file is the CI-side resolve of that file, not a
# replacement for it: the versions below all satisfy its floors, and
# PyGObject is pinned to the same 3.58.0 it already pins exactly.
#
# Installed with `pip install --require-hashes`, which refuses to install
# anything not listed here with a matching hash -- so the job gets the exact
# artifacts this file names, or it fails. Every transitive dependency is
# present because --require-hashes demands the whole closure; that is the
# point, not padding.
#
# Each version lists the sha256 of EVERY distribution PyPI publishes for it
# (wheels for each platform, plus the sdist). pip accepts a download that
# matches any one of them, so the pin does not quietly depend on the runner
# resolving to the same wheel this file was generated against. That is what
# lets ONE file serve all three OS jobs.
#
# The per-OS split is carried by markers rather than by three files: the
# macOS job takes the pyobjc-* closure, Windows takes pythonnet / clr-loader
# / cffi / pefile / pywin32-ctypes, Linux takes PyGObject / pycairo /
# python-xlib. A marker that matches nothing on any of the three runners
# (qtpy's `sys_platform == 'openbsd6'`, which pywebview declares) is kept
# rather than hand-deleted, so this file stays exactly what the resolver
# produced and a regeneration is a clean diff.
#
# SCOPE -- CPython 3.11 on macos-latest, windows-latest and ubuntu-latest,
# which is what all three jobs pin via actions/setup-python.
#
# PyGObject and pycairo are sdists, so Linux still BUILDS them; that is
# unchanged by this pin and is why the linux job apt-installs
# libgirepository1.0-dev / libgirepository-2.0-dev / libcairo2-dev /
# pkg-config first. Their PEP 517 build requirements are fetched into an
# isolated build env and are not themselves hash-checked -- that is pip's
# documented behaviour for build deps under --require-hashes, not a gap
# this file can close.
#
# The linux job keeps its `--ignore-installed`: if the runner image ever
# ships an apt python3-gi, pip's "already satisfied" check would otherwise
# skip building the PyGObject wheel that interpreter actually needs.
#
# Updating: Dependabot owns the routine bumps and rewrites the hashes along
# with the version, so a bump arrives already verifiable. A pin with no
# updater is the frozen end of the same problem an unpinned install is at
# the other end of. The updater is the `/.github/requirements` pip entry in
# .github/dependabot.yml, whose group pattern is `*` and so covers this file
# the day it lands. A bump here that raises a floor in
# desktop/requirements-dev.txt above what that file allows is the signal to
# update that file too.
#
# Generated with:
#   uv pip compile --generate-hashes --universal --python-version 3.11 \
#       desktop/requirements-dev.txt
#

    --hash=sha256:f3a22400bce1b0c701683820ac4f3b159cd301acab067c51c653e06961600597
    # via
    #   macholib
    #   pyinstaller
